claims.text: HEA components can be fabricated by laser powder bed fusion.
Conventional LPBF with static laser parameters produces high thermal gradients in HEA parts.
Static LPBF parameters cause residual stress, porosity, microcracks, and dimensional inaccuracies in HEA parts.
The proposed feedback system will use melt-pool temperature and geometry data to modify laser power and scan path in real time.
Real-time machine-learning control of laser power and scanning patterns will reduce melt-pool thermal gradients.
Reducing melt-pool thermal gradients will produce a more uniform solidification front.
A more uniform solidification front will produce a finer grain structure.
Reduced thermal gradients will lower residual-stress accumulation.
Reduced thermal gradients and more uniform solidification will minimize porosity and microcrack formation.
The selection or adjustment of favorable LPBF process parameters can improve fusion behavior in an HEA.
Continuous machine-learning adjustment will optimize melt-pool behavior and avoid excessively rapid cooling.
Avoiding excessive thermal gradients will prevent microstructural defects and dimensional distortion.
LPBF of HEAs typically involves high-energy, rapid-solidification conditions.
Relative to fixed-parameter LPBF, the feedback-controlled process will improve dimensional precision.
Relative to fixed-parameter LPBF, the feedback-controlled process will improve mechanical integrity.
Relative to fixed-parameter LPBF, the feedback-controlled process will reduce porosity, residual stress, and microstructural imperfections.
The intervention's effectiveness depends on the sensors and controller operating within their calibrated ranges.
Extreme process fluctuations or compromised sensor data may limit the effectiveness of feedback control.
The cited prior evidence supports the predicted direction of improvement from machine-learning feedback control.
